episode_title: Leadership, Burnout & Team Growth with Brittany Chappius | Ep. 138

real_qa.q: How did Be Well Massage and Aesthetics grow from a one-room solo practice to a 14-person spa business?
real_qa.r: Brittany Chappius started as a solo esthetician and massage therapist taking clients 45 hours a week. She rented a space that was originally advertised for splitting between two operators but negotiated with the landlord to take the entire house, then hired additional staff as people in the industry reached out wanting to work for her. The business expanded from one room to seven treatment rooms with a full team, with retention of employees from the beginning being notable in the spa industry.
real_qa.requete: Be Well Massage Aesthetics growth story

real_qa.q: What are the biggest challenges of transitioning from a solo spa practitioner to managing multiple employees?
real_qa.r: The hardest part for Brittany was learning to have challenging conversations with her team because she is very empathetic and had grown close relationships with long-term employees. She did not have a business background and was learning everything as she went. She emphasizes that your team is a direct reflection of your business, so managing them effectively while maintaining a supportive environment is critical, especially when people have worked with her for over five years.

real_qa.q: How does employee retention work at Be Well Massage and Aesthetics compared to typical spa businesses?
real_qa.r: Brittany attributes retention to knowing each individual team member deeply—how they learn, how they take criticism, and their personal circumstances—rather than fitting everyone into one box. She maintains a professional but personal relationship, ensuring her door is open for personal challenges. She has an all-female team that has formed lasting friendships, and clients sense and respond to this sisterly energy, making them want to return.

real_qa.q: What mindset shift did Brittany Chappius make about her identity as a business owner?
real_qa.r: Brittany realized that her business is not who she is and that she needed to have an identity and life outside of Be Well. She created stronger boundaries and learned to give herself grace instead of grinding constantly and being hard on herself. This shift came after she was overwhelmed, stressed, and lost passion in the business, and she discovered that prioritizing her own wellness through fitness and personal work made her a better business owner and leader.

real_qa.q: How did getting a fitness instructor certification help Brittany Chappius regain energy for her spa business?
real_qa.r: After becoming overwhelmed and losing passion, Brittany got her fitness instructor certification and began teaching classes at a startup. She says this reignited her passion for being a business owner by exposing her to new energy, different leadership approaches, and the drive of her startup employer. Teaching fitness also empowers women, allows her to work out, and markets Be Well—creating multiple wins while filling her cup and helping her overcome stage fright in leading team meetings.
real_qa.requete: fitness teaching as business owner fulfillment

real_qa.q: Why do business owners need external groups or mentorship to avoid getting stuck in their businesses?
real_qa.r: Nicole Overkamp, the host, notes that being in organizations like EO (Entrepreneurs' Organization) and surrounding yourself with other business owners prevents isolation and swampiness. Both she and Brittany agree that exposure to other entrepreneurs' energy and ideas helps iterate and improve your business. Brittany adds that she also coaches other business owners and finds that hearing their energy and drive reignites her own fuel and sparks new improvements in Be Well.

guest.bio_context: Brittany Chappius is an esthetician and massage therapist by trade who founded Be Well Massage and Aesthetics in 2017 in Williamsville, Western New York, starting as a solo practitioner in a single rented room. She has grown the business to a full-service wellness facility with 14 employees, seven treatment rooms, and a loyal client base. She also obtained her fitness instructor certification and teaches classes at a startup fitness company while continuing to lead her spa business and take select clients.
